page: Microsoft Azure D64nls_v6 is a network-optimized, low-memory virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is equipped with a dedicated Intel Xeon 8573C processor based on the x86_64 architecture, delivering 64 vCPUs across 32 physical cores with hyper-threading. Operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz, the processor features a 260 MB L3 cache. The instance is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, resulting in a low memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, but it is premium storage capable for external disk attachments.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong performance characteristics across compute and memory-bound workloads. The system achieves a strong Passmark CPU score of 67,502.06, supported by high-tier results in extended instructions, encryption, and physics simulations. Memory bandwidth is highly efficient, with read-only large block transfers reaching 244.26 GB/sec and write operations at 107.65 GB/sec, both placing in the top 25% of tested systems. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and single-threaded gzip compression also demonstrate strong throughput. For database operations, the instance exhibits high efficiency, processing 72.31 million Redis SET operations per second and scoring strongly in Passmark database tests.

The primary architectural tradeoff of the D64nls_v6 is its low memory density of 2.0 GB per vCPU, which limits its suitability for memory-intensive applications such as large in-memory databases. However, this resource allocation provides a cost-efficient profile for compute-heavy and network-bound tasks that do not require massive RAM footprints. The inclusion of Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 instructions enables strong performance in vector calculations and AI inference, as evidenced by strong prompt processing speeds across various LLM sizes. This instance is highly suited for network-optimized workloads, static web serving, high-throughput database operations, and compute-intensive batch processing.
